newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium at 2-1/2 year low as metals take a new hit.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium at 2-1/2 year low as metals take a new hit.

text.p: The price of aluminium dropped to a new 2-1/2 year low on Wednesday and copper was also under new pressure when speculators again bet that the industrial metals are not a hot investment just now. Other commodities could not compete with a surge in oil prices to post-Gulf War highs this week, as equities and bonds also continued to command speculative interest.

News of a big drop in warehouse copper stocks had triggered a rally on the price of that metal on Tuesday and it advanced almost to $1,950 a tonne. But copper has languished under a wave of negative sentiment since the disclosure earlier this year of huge losses by Japan's Sumitomo Corp on unauthorised dealing in the metal.

A bearish mood reasserted itself early on Wednesday and a new fall on copper, to an afternoon close at $1,928, added to pressure on aluminium. Last afternoon trade on aluminium was at $1,323 a tonne, down $23.50 from Tuesday. Traders said it may fall to $1,300 now.
Aluminium stocks are high and speculators doubt if the global economy is vigorous enough to stimulate strong new end-user demand.
Oil prices were firm around $24.50 a barrel for the benchmark North Sea Brent Blend of crude on tight supplies of heating oil in the run-up to the northern winter.

Brent futures hit $24.70 on Tuesday. Gold prices were firmer after silver rallied on news of a drop in U.S. stocks but the bullion market continued to be rangebound, traders said. Gold ended in London at $381.45 an ounce after $381.15 on Tuesday.
Coffee firmed with London Robusta type futures in a strong rebound helped by trade short-covering.

By the finish, most-active January was $35 a tonne higher at $1,488 while front-month November firmed $29 at $1,549. London cocoa futures registered small gains in late arbitrage buying against New York on Wednesday after a flat session. Sugar eased. Chicago wheat was little changed towards mid-session there.
